_comment: Mutation testing: breaks the source on purpose and checks the tests notice.
A mutant that leaves the suite green is a bug the tests cannot see — unlike line
coverage, this cannot be satisfied by executing code without asserting on it.
Two rules keep it usable:
1. NEVER gate a PR on this. A run re-executes the suite once per mutant, so it lives
in its own workflow (.github/workflows/mutation.yml), nightly and on demand.
2. Keep `mutate` pointed at logic. The generated `api/` directory, config and
infrastructure bootstrapping produce noise exclusively.
`jest.config.json`'s `coverageThreshold` mirrors the `mutate` array below: the same four
paths carry a 70% line/branch/function/statement floor, on the principle that logic worth
mutating is logic worth guaranteeing is executed at all. Mutation testing answers 'do the
tests assert anything', coverage answers 'do the tests run this at all' — the second is
the cheap check and it belongs in CI, where this does not. Keep the two lists in step.
(Matches the frontend, where the same pairing lives in `vitest.config.ts`.)
A run copies the whole project into `.stryker-tmp/sandbox-*`. `jest.config.json` ignores
that path in `testPathIgnorePatterns`/`modulePathIgnorePatterns`, because a plain `jest`
started while a run is in flight — or after a crashed one left the directory behind —
otherwise collects the copies as a second, duplicate suite: two suites competing for the
same in-memory Mongo, reporting failures against paths that are not the source tree.
Only the unit suite runs here. Integration and contract drive the real app over HTTP
against an in-memory Mongo; running either once per mutant would take hours and would
mostly re-measure what the unit suite already answers.
Thresholds come from a real run, not from a number invented in advance. Raise
`break` when the score rises; never lower it to make a run pass.
Measured 2026-08-08: 70.58% total / 78.24% of covered code, 1429 mutants, ~26 minutes
at the configured concurrency of 4 (~14 minutes at 8).
The two numbers moved apart because `# no cov` grew, not because assertions weakened:
`models/audit-logs.ts` (15.38%, 44 survivors) and `services/audit-logs.ts` (0%, 6 with no
coverage) arrived with the persisted audit trail and have no unit tests yet. They are the
single largest gap and the first place to spend effort.
A run strands one ~200 MB `mongo-mem-*` data directory in /tmp per killed worker (Stryker
SIGKILLs a jest worker per timed-out mutant, so `MongoMemoryServer.stop()` never runs).
`tests/helpers/global-setup.ts` sweeps them: every jest instance this run starts prunes
the directories whose `mongod` is provably gone, so a run reclaims its own strandings as
it goes instead of filling the tmpfs. It never touches a concurrent instance's live
directory — read that file before changing the sweep, the two verdicts are the design.
`ignorePatterns` must NOT list `public/**`, however tempting: the sandbox is the only
filesystem the tests see, and `tests/unit/db/seed-fixtures.test.ts` asserts that every
seed fixture's `imageUrl` resolves to a committed file under `public/images/seed/`. With
the directory left out of the copy, all of those fail and Stryker refuses to start at all
('failed tests in the initial test run'). `.gitignore` already keeps runtime uploads out,
and the committed remainder is under a megabyte.
Still worth attention, in rough order of payoff: services/products.ts (52.17%, 26 with
no coverage), services/users.ts (57.69%), services/auth.ts (53.19%), models/orders.ts
(51.43%), models/feedback-requests.ts (53.85%), models/users.ts (68.32%), and
models/user-validation.ts (40%). security.ts reports 0% because it is a bare rateLimit()
config object with no branch to exercise — leave it.
